summary: 十八世纪伦敦泥泞的街道原本不利步行，公共空间和路面改善后，步行风尚也发生变化。男女鞋的材料、耐用性与可见度反映不同活动期待，鞋履还标示阶层和男子成年的身份。

paragraphs.brief: 在上半个世纪，城市上层阶层的人身移动受到很大限制：街道条件差，不允许在私人公园或娱乐花园外 " 步行取乐 "。
sentences: It was difficult to get about in eighteenth-century London.
伦敦18世纪很难办到

During the first half of that century, the physical mobility of the upper classes in the city had been considerably restricted: the poor condition of the streets did not allow ‘walking for pleasure’ outside private parks or pleasure gardens.
在上半个世纪，城市上层阶层的人身移动受到很大限制：街道条件差，不允许在私人公园或娱乐花园外 " 步行取乐 "。
Streets were dirty, rubbish was everywhere and the British climate did not help.
街道脏，垃圾到处都是，英国的气候没有帮助。
Walking could be a risky business.
走路可能很危险
The terrible state of roads, always flooded and muddy, created a metropolitan world of shoe cleaners and street sweepers.
道路的可怕状况，总是淹水和泥巴，形成了一个清鞋和清扫街道的都市世界。

paragraphs.brief: 十八世纪初的教科书中没有提到步行问题。
sentences: References to walking are not abundant in early eighteenth-century texts.
十八世纪初的教科书中没有提到步行问题。
This is truer for urban spaces than for places in the countryside, where country life had always been dominated by a lifestyle of outdoor activities.
城市空间的情况比乡村地区的情况要好，乡村地区的生活一直以户外活动的生活方式为主。
For instance, in eighteenth-century London, a sightseer’s experience was restricted to touristic places and involved journeys by a series of boats and coaches.
例如，在十八世纪的伦敦，观光者的经验仅限于旅游地点，并有一系列船只和教练出行。
Walking was considered to be an activity for the poorer members of society — or simply those who could not afford a coach.
步行被认为是社会较贫穷成员的一项活动，或仅仅是那些无力支付教练费用的人的一项活动。

paragraphs.brief: 这种状况在十八世纪中叶突如其来的改善，采取了措施，提供可以步行的公共场所。
sentences: This situation underwent a sudden improvement in the mid-eighteenth century, with measures implementing the provision of public spaces in which to walk.
这种状况在十八世纪中叶突如其来的改善，采取了措施，提供可以步行的公共场所。
The first legislation concerning paving in London was passed in 1762, and during the following decades similar laws were enacted in many cities.
1762年，伦敦通过了第一部关于铺路的立法，随后几十年，许多城市颁布了类似的法律。
By the end of the century, areas for walking were commonplace, and far more people were enjoying the pastime than before.
到本世纪末，步行地区很普遍，享受消遣的人比以前多得多。
Sophie von La Roche writes about metropolitan street life in the diary of her visit to London of 1786.
苏菲·冯·拉罗什在1786年访问伦敦的日记中写到都市街头生活。

She comments on how many more pedestrians there were on the broad, clean pavements, alongside the houses where, she says ‘many thousands of neatly clad people, eminent men and dressy women, pursue their way safe from the carriages, horses and dirt’.
她评论说，在宽敞、清洁的街上还有多少行人，她说，“成千上万光滑的人、知名男子和着装的妇女，在马车、马匹和泥土中安全地走自己的路。”
Although the pastime of walking was pursued only in specific spaces designed for the purpose, the number of these spaces increased as the nineteenth century approached.
虽然行走的消遣只在为此目的设计的特定空间进行，但随着十九世纪的临近，这些空间的数量有所增加。
Travelling on foot became smoother and less dangerous.
徒步旅行变得比较平滑也比较危险

paragraphs.brief: 在时尚鞋类的实际设计中，可以看到对走过公共场所的态度及其随时间推移的变化。
sentences: Attitudes toward walking through public spaces and their changes over time were visible in the practical designs of fashionable footwear.
在时尚鞋类的实际设计中，可以看到对走过公共场所的态度及其随时间推移的变化。
Protective overshoes and other devices designed to keep feet above the dirty and wet ground soon disappeared, and ease of mobility increased.
旨在将脚放在肮脏和湿地之上的保护性超鞋和其他装置很快消失，行动方便度提高。
In the early eighteenth century, the look of men’s and women’s shoes started to diverge in appearance as a distinction between male and female footwear filtered into production.
18世纪初，男女鞋的外观开始不同，因为男女鞋的区别被过滤到生产中。
Contemporary descriptions of the boot and shoe trade underlined the differences between ladies’ shoemakers and men’s shoemakers too.
对鞋鞋业的当代描述也突显了女鞋匠和男鞋匠之间的差别。

paragraphs.brief: 男女鞋类的生产需要不同的技能，因为产品基本上是不同的。
sentences: The production of men’s and women’s footwear required different skills, as the products were essentially different.
男女鞋类的生产需要不同的技能，因为产品基本上是不同的。
Men wore more sober footwear, not unlike modern shoes.
男人穿得更清醒不像现代鞋
Their shoes were entirely made of leather, which provided resistance to rain, mud and bad weather.
他们的鞋子完全由皮革制成，对雨水、泥土和恶劣天气有抵抗力。
Women’s shoes had uppers made of textiles — silk, satin or cloth — and their resistance to bad weather and dirty streets was limited.
妇女的鞋上部有纺织品——丝绸、或布——她们对恶劣天气和肮脏街道的抵抗力有限。
Only the lower ranks of women wore leather shoes of a form similar to men’s.
只有下层妇女穿的皮鞋形式与男子相似。
The high-quality shoes for women were often embroidered and were normally worn with protective overshoes, as they were prone to being damaged or disfigured by the conditions of the time.
妇女穿的高品质鞋经常被刺绣，通常穿戴防护服，因为她们很容易因当时的状况而损坏或毁容。

paragraphs.brief: 男女的鞋子与她们更一般的服装有不同关系。
sentences: The shoes of men and women related to their more general clothing in different ways.
男女的鞋子与她们更一般的服装有不同关系。
Wealthy women’s footwear harmonised with their other garments, a harmony that could be effected through matching textiles, general colour, embroidered detail or buckles.
富裕妇女的鞋跟与其他衣服相协调，这种和谐可以通过将纺织品、普通颜色、刺绣细皮或扣子配对来实现。
In the eighteenth century, men’s shoes matched their clothing in different ways, for example with glossy black, red or pink heels.
在十八世纪，男子的鞋子以不同方式与衣服匹配，例如，黑、红或粉色高跟鞋。
The shoe of an upper-class man also acted as a type of sign which emphasised the difference between the wearer and young boys and women.
一名上层阶级男子的鞋也是一种标志，它强调磨衣者与男女青年之间的区别。
The shoe also distinguished him from working men who wore leather or cloth protective leggings, ragged shoes and clogs.
这双鞋还把他与那些穿皮革或布护腿、破鞋和木棍的工人区分开来。

The symbolic marking of the entry of a wealthy young man into manhood through his shoes, as well as his other dress, may have been of more importance than has previously been acknowledged in costume history.
一个有钱的年轻人通过鞋子和其他衣服进入男子状态的象征性标志可能比以前在服装史上承认的更重要。

items.en: details of a legal change affecting conditions in urban areas
items.zh: 影响城市地区条件的法律变化细节
items.why: C段记载1762年伦敦通过首部铺路法，随后多座城市仿效，属于改善市区条件的法律变化。

items.en: a reference to how the significance of men’s shoes has been overlooked by experts
items.zh: 专家如何忽视男子鞋的重要性
items.why: F段说鞋履可标志富裕少年成年，其意义或比服饰史过去承认的更大，正对应受到忽视。

items.en: a reference to how gender began to affect shoe design
items.zh: 提及性别如何开始影响鞋类设计
items.why: D段指出十八世纪初男女鞋的外观开始分化，标明性别差异开始体现在鞋款上。

items.en: a description of potential problems faced in urban areas
items.zh: 说明城市地区面临的潜在问题
items.why: A段写到街道肮脏、垃圾遍地，加上天气影响，这些都给市民出行造成困难。

items.en: a mention of the tough qualities of men’s shoes
items.zh: 提到男人的鞋的难看品质
items.why: 男鞋全用皮革制作，耐雨、泥泞与恶劣天气，体现其坚韧实用。

items.en: a reference to modes of transport used by visitors to London
items.zh: 提及访问伦敦的游客使用的运输方式
items.why: B段说十八世纪到伦敦观光的人在各景点之间乘船和坐马车，直接列出交通方式。

items.en: a mention of the limited areas in early eighteenth-century London where local people could enjoy walking
items.zh: 提到18世纪初伦敦的有限地区当地人可以享受步行
items.why: 早期街况差，能悠闲散步的地方限于私人公园和游乐花园。

items.en: The writer refers to the relationship between shoes and other clothing. Which TWO of the following are mentioned?
items.zh: 作者提到鞋子和其他服装之间的关系。以下两个方面有提及？
correct: Shoes for rich women were designed to match their dress in various ways.
为富人设计的鞋子可以以不同方式与衣服匹配。
Wealthy men’s shoes set the wearer apart from other groups.
富裕男子的鞋子把磨损器与其他群体分开。

items.en: In fact, in London, only people who were less well-off had to walk rather than take a ________.
items.zh: 实际上，在伦敦，只有经济较为拮据的人才不得不步行，因为他们坐不起________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“步行被认为是社会较贫穷成员的一项活动，或仅仅是那些无力支付教练费用的人的一项活动”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The situation, though, was different in the ________.
items.why: 前文说早期文本中很少提到步行，尤其是在城市中更是如但乡村不同，因为乡村生活本来就以户外活动为主。题干 The situation…was different in the…对应原文 plac in the countryside,所以答案是 countryside。

items.en: As a consequence, according to Sophie von La Roche, the number of ________ rose dramatically, because many people were able to walk on wide ____ (Q26) away from the traffic.
items.zh: 据索菲·冯·拉罗什记述，________的人数因此大幅增加，因为许多人可以沿着宽阔的________（Q26）行走，避开车流。
items.why: 题干中的 the number of…rose dramatically 对应原文 how many more pedestrians there were。这里指的是行人数量增加，因此答案是复数名词 pedestrians。

items.en: As a consequence, according to Sophie von La Roche, the number of ____ (Q25) rose dramatically, because many people were able to walk on wide ________ away from the traffic.
items.zh: 据索菲·冯·拉罗什记述，________（Q25）的人数因此大幅增加，因为许多人可以沿着宽阔的________行走，避开车流。
items.why: 回到对应内容“她评论说，在宽敞、清洁的街上还有多少行人，她说，“成千上万光滑的人、知名男子和着装的妇女，在马车、马匹和泥土中安全地走自己的路。””，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: D段指出十八世纪初男女鞋的外观开始分化，标明性别差异开始体现在鞋款上。
前文说早期文本中很少提到步行，尤其是在城市中更是如但乡村不同，因为乡村生活本来就以户外活动为主。题干 The situation…was different in the…对应原文 plac in the countryside,所以答案是 countryside。
clauses: Walking was considered to be an activity for the poorer members of society — or simply those ….
“who could not afford a coach”修饰前面的 those。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 those，再把修饰信息接回主句。
…, the number of these spaces increased as the nineteenth century approached.
连接词 although 引出“Although the pastime of walking was pursued only in specific spaces designed for the purpose”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。

观察鞋类和休闲的时尚变化
